target_customer: Midmarket corporate legal departments with large outside counsel spend
problem: In-house legal teams tracked outside counsel invoices and matters in spreadsheets and email, with little view of spend. SimpleLegal offered e-billing, matter, vendor and spend analytics in one simple tool.
business_model: B2B SaaS subscription for corporate legal departments
product_category: Legal operations software (e-billing, spend and matter management)

founders.name: Patrik Outericky
founders.background_notes: YC profile says he built much of the initial product and cites BI and analytics experience at an enterprise SaaS startup.

founders.name: Nathan Wenzel
founders.background_notes: Named as CEO in Above the Law (2017) and the Onit announcement; a personal page says he founded the company, not independently verified. Not listed on the YC page.

technical_complexity.rationale: Web SaaS built on Python and Django with invoice parsing and reporting; standard engineering with some data integration work.

defensibility.rationale: Invoice and matter history plus workflow integration create switching costs once adopted, but the feature set is replicable and incumbents were established.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Incumbents did not crush it. SimpleLegal grew to about 60 staff and sold to Onit in 2019, after Onit received a 200M investment from K1.

market_need_then: Corporate legal departments faced growing pressure to control outside counsel spend and relied on manual tracking; no dated spend figures were found.

branding.name_origin: The founders chose the name because simplicity is part of the company identity and keeping the product simple takes ongoing effort (company blog post, 2016).
branding.domain_note: Used simplelegal.com; it now redirects to Onit.

identity.voice_and_tone: Plain, simplicity focused, culture of curiosity and empathy per its own pages

branding.community_and_virality: Podcast and legal press coverage; no evidence of a community or merch.

brand_strength.rationale: Clear name that fits the promise, but generic and similar to other legal brands (SimpleLaw); no evidence it drove growth.

outcome_analysis: SimpleLegal built a simple legal spend and matter product for midmarket legal departments, raised a 10M Series A led by Emergence in 2017 and was acquired by Onit in May 2019. The sale came alongside a large private equity investment into Onit, a consolidation pattern in legal tech. Sources do not state the price, so the outcome is a clean exit of unknown size after the Series A.
notes: Series A amount and date confirmed by Above the Law (June 2017) and startupintros snippet. CB Insights lists about 11.7M total over 6 rounds; earlier seed rounds not itemized. Exit date from the Onit release; a database listing of Sept 2025 looks wrong. No competitor sources dated near 2013 were found.
